candidates.title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment
candidates.summary: Language model (LM) alignment improves model outputs to reflect human preferences while preserving the capabilities of the base model. The most common alignment approaches are (i) reinforcement learning, which maximizes the expected reward under a KL-divergence constraint, and (ii) best-of-NNN alignment, which selects the highest-reward output among NNN independent samples. Despite their widespread use, the fundamental limits of reward improvement under a KL budget remain poorly understood. candidates.title: ggml-org/llama.cpp release: b12558
candidates.summary: <details open> vulkan: disable subgroup arithmetic on Qualcomm's driver (#30826) On Adreno, subgroupAdd() after divergent code returns wrong sums. The fused ADD+RMS_NORM partial-sum path hits this, so the decode-step norm is garbage and models emit stray tokens after long prompts. Clear subgroup_arithmetic for the Qualcomm proprietary driver, which also turns off add_rms_fusion and the other subgroupAdd paths. test-backend-ops on Adreno 850 and X2-90: ADD_RMS_NORM 20/25 -> 25/25, RMS_NORM_MUL_ADD 33/45 -> 45/45. llama 3B Q4_0 on Adreno 850: pp512 and tg128 unchanged. </details> **Website:** -

candidates.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
candidates.summary: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory.
